compose_runtime.purpose: Differential validation of the zero-argument Unit Compose callback ABI using the Compose compiler plugin bundled with the pinned Kotlin compiler

limitations: Only literal zero-argument Unit composable callbacks and straight-line calls to public static noninline nongeneric Unit composable functions from Kotlin file facades are lowered; source composable declarations and class/member/receiver/suspend/vararg/generic/result-returning call shapes remain unsupported

Calls accept up to64 logical parameters with the exact pinned Composer/changed/default mask descriptor; static expressions include supported literals, singletons and @Stable producers with static arguments. Conditional composable calls/exits, mixed fixed appliers, inferred/open target schemes and callback type target schemes reject explicitly
Nested ordinary function creation and plugin memoization remain explicitly unsupported in this snapshot
Runtime protocol is pinned to AndroidX Compose Runtime1.11.0 and Kotlin2.3.21 bundled plugin; keys and generated class names are compiler-specific

Composer/RecomposeScope are controlled proxies; actual composableLambdaInstance wrappers and pinned composable callee bytecode execute, without a real Composition/Recomposer or Android execution claim
ASM method-entry probes preserve descriptors, Kotlin metadata and bodies of actual pinned callees and record hidden arguments; runtime classpath excludes compiler/ASM jars

features.name: Straight-line transformed binary composable Unit calls

controlled_app_recheck.scope: resolves transformed callee and its arguments, then explicitly rejects required nested callback memoization

validation.note: The immutable compiler binary and original bundled inputs remain authoritative. Validation-only patch adds two cfg(test) initializer defaults and the same pure Option::or Clippy/format correction already committed by peers; these do not change Compose production lowering.
